1201.author: Sheila Sta. Maria
1201.body:
Pada tanggal 12 Februari 2014, fenomena yang tidak dapat dijelaskan terjadi ketika serangkaian bencana alam melanda berbagai wilayah di dunia secara bersamaan selama enam jam. Kini dikenal sebagai The Ruling atau The Judgment, peristiwa ganas ini menyebabkan resesi ekonomi global dan kerugian internasional yang mencapai total hingga $20 triliun.

Terdiri dari gempa bumi, tsunami, tornado, dan badai tropis, terdapat 308 bencana alam yang tercatat terkait dengan The Ruling. Wilayah dan daerah yang terdampak mengalami kerusakan parah, termasuk dua keajaiban dunia yang kini tidak dapat diperbaiki. Bencana ini telah menyebabkan banyak negara mengalami kondisi ekstrem, mulai dari pengangguran massal hingga kelaparan yang meluas.

Saat ini, para ahli meteorologi dan seismologi di seluruh dunia belum memiliki penjelasan logis mengenai letusan bencana yang terjadi secara tiba-tiba. Berbagai hipotesis telah diajukan dan sedang diteliti, seperti spekulasi para fisikawan kuantum yang menganggapnya sebagai hasil tabrakan multiverse berdasarkan interpretasi Everett.

Di Filipina, yang dianggap sebagai salah satu negara "beruntung", dua gempa bumi dan satu badai tropis melanda negara tersebut, terutama di wilayah utara dan selatan. Meskipun jumlah bencana alam relatif lebih sedikit, dampaknya masih terasa hingga saat ini. Wilayah perkotaan dan kota metropolitan, bagaimanapun, tidak terkena dampaknya. Badan Statistik Nasional (NSB) melaporkan hingga 461.000 korban sipil dan kerugian hingga Php 940 miliar.

Seperti kebanyakan negara dunia ketiga, Filipina masih berada dalam keadaan darurat, dengan Presiden Fernando Cojuangco memiliki wewenang eksekutif khusus sejak peristiwa tersebut.

[b]9 Februari.[/b] Daerah tekanan rendah (LPA) berkembang di sebelah timur Wilayah Tanggung Jawab Filipina (PAR).

[b]11 Februari.[/b] LPA berkembang dengan cepat. PAGASA melihatnya sebagai angin tropis, kemudian menjadi badai topan pada hari yang sama, dan memberi nama "Halanda". Diprediksi akan melanda wilayah barat laut dalam hitunga jam, warga sipil segera dievakuasi.

[b]12 Februari pukul 2.16 pagi.[/b] Gempa bumi pertama melanda Strasbourg, Prancis, menandai dimulainya serangkaian bencana.

[b]12 February pukul 3.12 pagi.[/b] Gempa bumi 8,2 magnitudo melanda wilayah utara, dengan pusat gempa berada di Brgy. Panpan, Makarito, berlangsung selama 1 menit dan 12 detik, diikuti oleh 2 gempa susulan.

[b]12 February pukul 3.29 pagi.[/b] Badai "Halanda" dengan cepat mencapai kecepatan angin hingga 220 km/jam, menyerang wilayah barat laut.

[b]12 February pukul 4.08 pagi.[/b] Gempa bumi 7,8 magnitudo melanda wilayah selatan, dengan pusat gempa berada di Brgy. Buwanan, Santoro, berlangsung selama 1 menit dan 36 detik, diikuti oleh 3 gempa susulan.

[b]12 February.[/b] Presiden Fernando Cojuangco menyatakan negara dalam keadaan darurat. Kongres dengan cepat memberikan presiden wewenang eksekutif khusus untuk "tanggapan darurat segera."

[b]13 Februari.[/b] Kepolisian Nasional Filipina (PNP) mengerahkan hingga 7.000 personel dan kendaraan lapis baja, mendirikan pos pemeriksaan, dan memberlakukan jam malam untuk membantu mencegah penjarahan.

[b]14 Februari.[/b] Departemen Pembangunan Sosial dan Kesejahteraan (DSDW) memperkirakan lebih dari 5,2 juta keluarga, atau sekitar 25,1 juta individu (sekitar 1/4 dari populasi), terdampak oleh The Ruling.

[b]15 Februari.[/b] Dewan Nasional Pengurangan Risiko Bencana dan Penanggulangan Bencana (NDRRMC) melaporkan bahwa jumlah korban tewas awal mencapai 284.000 orang, dengan mayoritas korban berasal dari Makarito, Panguina, dan Carlosan.

[b]16 Februari.[/b] Senat mempertimbangkan dana rehabilitasi sebesar P49 miliar untuk korban. Ketua Komite Keuangan Senat, Norbert Cupitero, menjanjikan bahwa Senat akan menerapkan langkah-langkah pengamanan untuk "memastikan dana tersebut tidak akan jatuh ke tangan para korup."

[b]17 Februari.[/b] Cojuangco menyampaikan pidato mengenai upaya renovasi yang sedang berlangsung, dengan menyoroti renovasi besar-besaran dari satu jembatan penyeberangan di Makarito senilai P15 juta.

[b]19 Februari.[/b] Menteri Kesehatan Frankie Santos IX mengumumkan rencana untuk pengecatan ulang rumah sakit di kota-kota besar, dengan mengatakan bahwa "dinding yang baru dicat penting untuk kesejahteraan pasien." Ketika ditanya tentang renovasi rumah sakit provinsi yang hancur, Santos keluar dari konferensi.

[b]23 Februari[/b]. Setelah munculnya beberapa laporan berita internasional yang mengkritik respons krisis negara, terjadi arus masuk bantuan asing dari negara-negara tetangga dan organisasi nirlaba. Juru Bicara Presiden Roberto Quimpo memuji para pemimpin dunia atas bantuan keuangan tersebut, dan menyerang para jurnalis atas kritik mereka yang "tidak berdasar."

[b]25 Februari.[/b] Senat menaikkan anggaran untuk pekerjaan rehabilitasi, perbaikan, dan konstruksi di daerah terdampak menjadi P69 miliar. Cupitero menegaskan kembali metodologi anti-korupsi dan menjamin distribusi dana dan bantuan yang lancar.

[b]2 Maret.[/b] Santos mengumumkan proyek penelitiannya yang mendapat kritik tajam tentang hibrida mangga-pisang. "Setelah bangun dari mimpi, sekarang saya tahu cara menyelamatkan negara ini dari krisis bodoh ini," ujar Santos.

[b]8 Maret.[/b] PBB turut merasakan kekecewaan korban lokal atas distribusi bantuan yang "sangat lambat" ke daerah-daerah yang hancur akibat The Ruling.

[b]17 Maret.[/b] Cojuangco menyampaikan pidato singkat membahas lima proyek renovasi jembatan pejalan kaki yang telah selesai tepat waktu.

[b]18 Maret.[/b] Para ahli di Universitas Filipina (PU) memperkirakan akan terjadi 300.000 kematian pada awal April jika upaya bantuan yang "terus-menerus kurang memadai" ini terus berlanjut, terutama disebabkan oleh kurangnya akses ke layanan kesehatan, layanan esensial, air, dan makanan.

[b]20 Maret.[/b] Jubir Presiden Roberto Quimpo menantang ketahanan rakyat Filipina terhadap prediksi PU. "Ayo buktikan PU salah! Berpuasa sedikit lebih lama. Kita satu hati dalam hal ini dan kita tidak akan mencapai 300.000 kematian pada 1 April," ujar Quimpo.

[b]1 April.[/b] Di tengah meningkatnya tingkat pengangguran dan kelangkaan pangan, NDRRMC melaporkan bahwa jumlah korban tewas telah mencapai 290.000. "Itudia! Kita menang! Kita mengalahkan prediksi PU. Angkanya sangat tipis, tetapi kita baru saja secara statistik membuktikan kompetensi tak terbantahkan dari pemerintah kita," ujar Quimpo.

[b]18 April.[/b] Presiden Cojuangco mengungkapkan bahwa rencana krisis utama yang dinantikan akhirnya memasuki tahap perencanaan awal. "Akhirnya, dua bulan setelah bencana, saya umumkan bahwa kami kini sedang merencanakan cara untuk memastikan tingkat keberhasilan yang sangat tinggi di semua bidang dan sektor." ujar Cojuangco.

[b]4 Mei.[/b] NDRRMC melaporkan bahwa jumlah korban tewas telah mencapai 348.000.

[b]23 Mei.[/b] Quimpo mengumumkan penundaan dalam tahap pra-perencanaan, dengan klaim bahwa proses tersebut mungkin perlu waktu 2-3 minggu lagi sebelum Dewan Rencana Darurat memasuki tahap perencanaan.

[b]27 Mei.[/b] Jumlah warga sipil yang meninggalkan zona evakuasi melonjak hingga mencapai rekor, dipicu oleh laporan kekurangan kebutuhan dasar dan layanan.

[b]13 Juni.[/b] Menyusul peringatan Hari Kemerdekaan, Cojuangco mengumumkan perpanjangan wewenang eksekutifnya dan peralihan rencana darurat krisis ke tahap perencanaan. "Dewan telah mengambil setiap langkah dan tindakan yang cermat untuk memastikan kesiapan saat pelaksanaan." ujar Cojuangco.

[b]19 Juli.[/b] NDRRMC melaporkan bahwa jumlah korban tewas telah mencapai 402.000.

[b]10 Agustus.[/b] Menanggapi warga sipil yang meninggalkan area evakuasi, Cojuangco mengumumkan pembangunan Unit Kantor Tanggap Krisis (CROU) di kota-kota dan kabupaten di wilayah terdampak, yang akan menyediakan bantuan dan dukungan terpusat bagi unit evakuasi.

[b]2 September.[/b] Menurut laporan nasional, CROU terbukti berhasil dalam meningkatkan efisiensi penyaluran bantuan. Selain itu, terdapat penurunan upaya pengabaian dan kondisi hidup yang lebih baik di kalangan korban dan pengungsi. Namun, para ahli dan kritikus menyoroti bahwa akses terhadap layanan kesehatan yang layak masih sangat terbatas.

[b]6 September.[/b] Meskipun penolakan terus-menerus terhadap evakuasi massal permanen sebagai langkah konkret, Quimpo akhirnya mengumumkan bahwa "RUU Evakuasi Permanen" telah disahkan menjadi undang-undang.

[b]8 September.[/b] Setelah rekonstruksi jembatan pejalan kaki, lampu lalu lintas, dan lubang inspeksi, renovasi dan pembangunan unit perumahan dimulai untuk evakuasi massal permanen, kemudian jalan tol dan jalan raya akan menyusul hingga tahun 2015. Quimpo memamerkan kemajuan yang terus membaik dan mengklaim bahwa mereka memahami prioritas mereka dengan baik.

8342.author: Sheila Sta. Maria
8342.body:
World economy has started to recover after the disastrous impact of The Ruling, United Countries Department of Economic and Social Affairs released a report on Monday, citing business activity indicators following world leaders' rehabilitation efforts focused on job employment.

UC DESA commended world leaders because of their program pointing out the process of economic adaptation and adjustment focusing on rehabilitation programs and job offerings to their citizens.

"This new analysis shows a very significant economic impact of the new policies and rules rolled out by governments and WBDO in response to the recession," said UC DESA Chief Economist Masamuri Takeda. "It also features that the vital role policy interventions can aid in mitigating incremental damage to economies. These findings can provide governments a next plan of action to fully recover their respective economy and lessen the impacts of The Ruling on their economies and people."

The Ruling triggered the recession earlier this year causing the global economy to suffer $18.6 trillion in losses—equivalent to 7.8% to 11.4% of global domestic product (GDP).

While world economy is suffering the worst recession on record in 2014 of up to 15.8%, World Bank De Oro predicts that sustainable recovery would start in the first quarter of the upcoming year, with GDP likely to bounce back and grow by 4.7% to 9.1% next year.

However, it is expected that the debt-to-GDP ratio of third-world countries will hit the ceiling and predicted to creep past 80% in average of their GDP. UC DESA report indicates that it is caused by injudicious spending policies set in place by the respective governments that kept each country's macroeconomic fundamentals weak.

4498.author: Kenneth Aragones
4498.body:
Dubbed as the Philippines' food capital, Liamson City is well-known as one of the best places in the country to satisfy your taste buds. There are so many restaurants and street vendors selling delicious food that it can sometimes get difficult to spot the exceptional ones. What we want are places that serve authentic and delicious food, where the Liamsoneños themselves savor the flavor and keep coming back to.

[center][b]HALO-HALO[/b][/center]

The go-to places for comfort food, Doring's listed its halo-halo a dessert fare. Not just mixed with toppings, a big chunk of sweet and soft leche flan is nestled in between the bananas, ube halaya, nata de coco, sweet beans, and coarse ice. With generous amounts of all the ingredients mixed in together, Doring's halo-halo is perfect for those who want a filling version of the local dessert.

[center][b]LUGAW[/b][/center]

This served in a ceramic bowl, the dish comes with no more than bits of fried minced garlic, chopped chives, and a piece of calamansi. This dish is great for budget-conscious individuals looking for a quick snack. It gives you a bang for your buck especially if you order the dish with their crunchy "okoy".

[center][b]PALITAW[/b][/center]

The neighboring municipality of Bonifacio is known for its kakanin. However, there is one woman who defied the title. Tarciana Reyes was a 75-year-old vendor of tasty palitaw and galapong for almost 40 years in Taytay, specifically beside the Liamson Memorial Stadium. Biko and galapong are sold in almost every market. They are sold in bilaos along with other kakanins like sapin-sapin. Biko is basically rice cakes topped with latik--the crunchy and sweet remains made from caramelizing coconut milk and sugar, while galapong is usually dipped in a specially made sauce from coconut milk as well. A slice of biko or galapong would surely go well with a cup of coffee or perhaps tea.

[center][b]SINIGANG NA KANDULI[/b][/center]

Starting as a circle of friends building a mini eatery, Bahay Kamayan had risen up to a famous restaurant in Downtown Liamson visited even by people from faraway places along Metro and even other provinces like Dolor, Mananita, and Kantos. At Bahay Kamayan, they give that brand new experience of enjoying foods you've never tried before such as kandule (also known as catfish). Sinigang na Kandule sa Miso is Bahay Kamayan's tasteful version of sour soup, as well as their trademark recipe. Mixed with vegetables and sour soup, you'll surely love this not-so-common dish served on the table. Though disliked by a lot of people, they have a flavorful version capable of changing minds.

[center][b]BARBEQUE[/b][/center]

For cheap thrills, Mang Gerry's pork barbeque offers hefty slices of lean pork meat skewered on the stick with little fat. A small cramped place without parking, their pork barbeque is still worth the wait. Tender even with some charred edges, Mang Gerry's barbeque version is a perfect match with vinegar dip with onions.

6969.author: Althea K. Lucente
6969.body:
Health Sec. Frankie Santos IX announced that the first stage of testing mango-banana hybrids on humans has recently begun. Despite active criticism from the scientific and academic community, Santos affirms the public with claims of its "incredible medical power capable of healing any illness and disorder, including conceptual ones like current economic problems." Furthermore, he consistently claims that drinking water will heighten its effects.

The testing has allegedly been delayed by a month due to difficulties in finding test subjects, but Santos assured the public that his volunteering subjects will be safe from harm and enjoy massive lifetime financial assistance.

"While you are all pestering me to resign from my post, you shall be regretful of such sayings once this blessing is disseminated to every doorstep," Santos said in a statement, citing criticisms from local celebrities, icons, and experts urging him to resign. Amid concerns on renovating hospitals and medical institutions destroyed by The Ruling, Santos states that renovation shouldn't be a top priority.

Through a breakthrough in genome research known as CRISPY, the secretary's head research team was able to conflate the genetic code of native mangoes and bananas. After numerous trials and burning half of the department's budget, the team announced its first successful trial in September 2014. Shortly after, the department made #MangoBananaDanceChallenge a nationwide viral trend, promoting its potential and future consumption through dance videos.

The research for the fruit breeding project launched in March 2014, about one month after The Ruling, after a "realization from a dream" by Dr. Santos.

1435.author: Kiko Espadero
1435.body:
The inter-agency task force for "The Ruling" recovery is eyeing to complete first quarter next year all housing projects and renovations intended for the survivors, including 15,000 classrooms and one footbridge renovation project worth P20 million, Pres. Fernando Cojuangco said during an interview.

Under the National Housing Department (NHD), about 50% of the proposed 205,128 housing units intended for The Ruling victims are now completed and set to turn over this coming January to affected families and, in addition, the government will add another 100,000 housing units using next year's national budget.

"Our original target was to complete all housing projects by the end of 2014, but realistically, we cannot do that because 2014 is about to end. So our target now is to complete all housing projects by first quarter of 2015 and add 100,000 more units, not only in nearby provinces but also in remote areas and Island Region since they're the ones most affected by those hurricanes and earthquakes," President Cojuangco told reporters.

NHD Sec. Gerald Marcelino Jr. said on an interview that each row house will have one bedroom, granite floor, and an area of 30 square meters, that can accommodate one family with at most 8 members, wider than the existing relocation units with only a 22-square-meter floor area.

The government is implementing strict compliance with the specification for contractors completing "The Ruling" housing projects to ensure housing quality. However, engineers pointed out that the timeline given by the NHD on project completion doesn't match to the standard building time of at least a one-story cemented house.

"For the meantime, my beloved countrymen, please bear with this temporary housing unit. Yes, we are not proud of its durability, but for the mean time, it is better than sleeping on the floor of covered courts. We are doing our best so please just help and cooperate," Pres. Cojuangco added.

According to latest statistics from national reports, the total damage cost and losses in areas affected by The Ruling has reached Php 938.5 billion.

3874.author: Jillian Calangi
3874.body:
Police Chief Gen. Somara Buendia on Thursday questioned Health Secretary Dr. Frankie Santos IX on the purchase of 1 million sets of vaccine kits at Php 2,500 each, compared to its average market value of around Php 1,000.

In an inter-agency meeting, Gen. Buendia pointed out the health department procurement of immunization vaccine kits worth Php 2,500 each, which is almost triple the price of that offered by Sanoly Pharma Corporation which costs Php 800.

"Dr. Santos, I demand an answer. Forget about your pointless fruit breeding project. The scientific consensus denies your claims, and thus, you're deluded. Now, I'm asking you to address this issue summoned by some of our fellow citizens," Buendia said in a statement.

Senate Leader Gladys Ramos said the chamber could not also understand why the health department has to pay this "unbelievable amount" for the vaccination kits and why there is such discrepancy between the prices. She also stressed that the government can cut the cost of vaccine kits along with other medical supplies if purchased directly from manufacturers.

Buendia told BTS Philippines that she is now looking at the possibility of filing charges against Santos and suggested to Pres. Fernando Cojuangco that the health efforts of the government in 2015 should be managed by the health division of the Philippine Army.

"We need to investigate this issue but I don't think it's our utmost priority. We should focus our attention and efforts to the rehabilitation of our country and helping our resilient countrymen overcome the challenges brought by the crisis," President Cojuangco said in his meeting closing speech.

7938.author: Sheila Sta. Maria
7938.body:
Basic Development Assistance Fund (BDAF) was designed to allow lawmakers to back small-scale community or infrastructure projects outside the scope of national large-scale infrastructure programs. It was formally enacted into law by former president Josephine Sumulong in 1989. Formerly named as National Development Fund (NDF), it was renamed by former president and film star Joshua Ducot to BDAF in 1999.

The allocated budget for each legislator kept ballooning from term to term, going from 20 billion pesos during Gracie Macapal's term to 40 billion pesos during incumbent Pres. Cojuangco's term. Over the years, its constitutionality had been questioned by the Supreme Court, where legislators are often polarized on its abolition, some of whom had recently been indicted for their involvement in the BDAF scandal.

[b]September 1989.[/b] NDF established during the administration of Josephine Sumulong.

[b]May 1999.[/b] Renamed to BDAF during the term of Joshua Ducot.

[b]February 2000.[/b] Its constitutionality is challenged; SC ruled the BDAF as constitutional.

[b]December 2000.[/b] Sulong News published an exposé elaborating systemic corruption revolving around BDAF.

[b]March 2, 2001.[/b] Public outrage over its alleged misuse sparked.

[b]March 18, 2001.[/b] Its constitutionality is reaffirmed; ruling retained as constitutional.

[b]June 5, 2001.[/b] Along with the 2001 corruption charges and scandals, public rage sparked protests that led to the impeachment of Joshua Ducot later that year.

[b]April 19, 2009.[/b] Numerous documents of "ghost" non-government organizations were leaked, suspected as being used for plunder with BDAF.

[b]July 30, 2013.[/b] News outlets reported 10 billion pesos from BDAF allegedly channeling into ghost projects and non-profits over the past 20 years. The mastermind of the scam, believed to be a businesswoman, remains unknown.

[b]August 20, 2013.[/b] Pres. Fernando Cojuangco announced a P69 million reward for information exposing whoever the mastermind of the BDAF scam is.

[b]September 2, 2013[/b]. "Pork barrel queen" Jhen Francisco surrendered to the Office of the President, wanted on charges of plunder and serious illegal detention. Netizens were wondering who won the P69M reward.

[b]November 7, 2013.[/b] Jhen Francisco refused to answer questions during a senate hearing. Shortly after, the anti-graft court declares Francisco as state witness, sparking mass protests. She was put under state protection and cleared of all charges in exchange for full cooperation.

[b]November 16, 2013.[/b] During another senate hearing, Francisco released evidence, documents, and a list of 69 politicians and entrepreneurs involved in the scam, famously dubbed as "Francisco 69."

[b]November 24, 2013[/b]. The Supreme Court finally rules BDAF as unconstitutional, stating that remaining allocated funds for BDAF will go back to Treasury.

[b]January 29.[/b] The Supreme Court and National Commission of Investigation rule the information, including Francisco 69, as valid and legitimate. 5 senators were charged of graft, corruption, and plunder.

[b]April 2.[/b] The National Commission of Investigation starts discovering more information, stating that "this is more profound and intricate than we had imagined."

[b]April 14.[/b] Sulong News published an exposé on the reallocation of remaining funds from BDAF to suspiciously overpriced projects, claiming that the funds never returned to Treasury.

[b]May 6.[/b] The head of the Office of Treasury denied such claims and slams Sulong News with a controversial remark "Shut yourselves down, you f****** monkeys."

9969.author: Jillian Calangi
9969.body:
It looks like this nation isn't yet tired of having actors of blockbuster films rule over the country. After his widespread efforts for The Ruling victims praised all over social media, Manuel Sikatin surprised the people upon announcing his early plans to run for presidency in an exclusive one-on-one interview on live television.

Out of the 19 Philippine presidents, 9 of them are either film stars or popular local icons with no political background. With a huge fan base and an empowered backing thanks to his philanthropy and humanitarian efforts, the famously dubbed "Hero Boy of Alcantara" might just become the 10th film star taking the presidential seat after Incumbent Pres. Fernando Cojuangco.

Sikatin said in the interview, "I don't care what they say. People love me. I know nothing about leadership, but hey, as long as I've got deep pockets, what could go wrong?" However, at the same time, he expressed disinterest and uncertainty, saying "It's still 2 years from now. Anything could change. I might star in the sequel of Hero Boy and give up presidency. But, for now, my eyes are on that seat."

Netizens expressed their mixed reactions on social media. Some of whom are praising Manuel Sikatin for being bold to extrapolate his crime-fighting skills in Hero Boy to national leadership, indulging in the possibility of a country devoid of crime like that in Hero Boy. The other side condemns such an act, claiming it as impulsive and unwise.

Sikatin has provided relief goods, food packs, supplies, and housing for about a quarter of the provincial areas affected by The Ruling, which is considered by many to be the best effort in mitigating damages, even more so than the national government. With a reported net worth of 10 billion pesos, the Hero Boy of Alcantara promises to reach more areas and supply aid.

3193.author: Kenneth Aragones
3193.body:
Our fight for a greener earth has resulted in various creative solutions such as "Live in Trash Advocacies", banning of plastic bags and the use of electric vehicles (EVs). Study shows the latter, though great in many aspects, does virtually nothing when dealing with global warming.

The 2012 comprehensive life-cycle analysis in an acclaimed journal shows that almost half of the lifetime carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions of an EV came from its production alone, especially the production of lithium batteries. In fact, when a single EV rolls off the production line, it is already responsible for a staggering 30,000 pounds of CO2 emissions. The amount of CO2 emission used to make a typical conventional car is 14,000 pounds.

Meanwhile, the burning of fossil fuels for transportation is accounted as the second largest source of CO2 emissions. Regarding this, transportation is responsible for the 26% of total greenhouse emission worldwide in 2013. At the same time, fossil fuel dependence has become such a huge problem, but promoting the use of electric cars, especially if it's done in a wide scale, could surely solve it, as it doesn't use that much fuel.

EVs run on rechargeable batteries instead of fossil fuels. EV batteries need to be replaced every three to ten years depending on its quality and usage but they can wear out and may need to be replaced immediately. Battery disposal, whether from a conventional vehicle or an electric one, is likely hazardous.

A battery itself is safe, but precautions apply in its disposal, since it contains lead — a toxic metal known to cause brain damage, deafness, blindness and even death. Many countries labeled lead acid as a hazardous toxic material. It can enter the body by inhalation and ingestion. Cadmium and sulfuric acid are other harmful chemicals found in batteries.

The biggest environmental advantage of owning an electric car, however, may also be its major drawback. EVs run on electricity, while electricity is produced mainly by burning fossil fuels and coal. Transportation, as mentioned, is the second largest source of CO2. Unfortunately, electricity is the largest source of it. In fact, electricity production and use are accounted for 37% of CO2 emission worldwide.

Even if an electric car is charged using clean energy, the car will only cause 24% less CO2 emission than conventional car. Certainly a far cry from their "Zero Carbon Dioxide Emission" tagline. EVs have higher manufacturing emission than normal cars. They also use lead batteries and, obviously, they depend on electricity which as we know has its own carbon footprint. Summing up, these clearly contradict any climate benefit of EVs.

1432.author: Kiko Espadero
1432.body:
During the press conference, Presidential Spokesperson Roberto Quimpo read the statement of President Fernando Cojuangco regarding the government efforts on helping all the victims of the sequential and simultaneous catastrophes that happened earlier this year.

"Food packs and other needs of the victims will be duly provided by the government as headed by Secretary Marie Josie Gumaca. Relocation sites have been constructed from the ground up and are now being prepared for permanent occupancy," Quimpo stated.

"Our President is also urging the Senate and Congress to grant extended special powers to the Executive Branch in order to further strengthen our response and recovery," Quimpo added. If ever such a request is approved, this would be the third time President Cojuangco is extending his special powers that has now been lasting for 10 months.

Quimpo also assured that renovation efforts are still ongoing, after being delayed by challenges in logistics and transportation, considering that some areas are totally unreachable by land due to irreparably destroyed highways and bridges.

Despite these recent efforts, many citizens are criticizing the "lack of sense of urgency of the government" in handling the crisis due to the very slow response in mitigating damages to infrastructure, life, and sustainability.

"Mass permanent evacuation is happening at last, but it's already been 10 months. Imagine how many of our countrymen have starved to death. Remember that most people affected by The Ruling are living in poverty," the head of youth organization AKTO criticized in an online statement.

2410.author: Jillian Calangi
2410.body:
Even after a year since the abolishment of Basic Development Assistance Fund (BDAF), the National Commission of Investigation is continually exposing more and more politicians and businessmen involved in the BDAF pork barrel scandal, most of whom are racking millions of pesos in their accounts and setting local records in tax evasion. Political analyst Richie Darwin stated in an interview "Even a teacher's average annual tax is more than all of these politicians' tax filings combined."

After the turn of these recent events divulging the system, Securities and Exchange Commission Director Harold Venecia speaks up and expresses fears for the country's future and demands good governance from the Executive Branch including President Fernando Cojuangco.

He states that the country might soon become a hotspot for money laundering if the system thrives for longer. "Not just a local hotspot, but an international one. If this lingers on, we'll have officials all around the world illegally circulating money thanks to our ignorance and incompetence," Venecia stated after expressing concerns about foreign nationals being unexpectedly involved in the scandal.

Venecia specifically addressed his demands to the Executive Branch and President Cojuangco to "wipe this corrupted system clean" and "be transparent with everything." Venecia also discussed about fixing up improper legislation that leads to opportunistic loopholes.

Many netizens are praising Venecia for having the courage to speak up. Most of them specifically point out they've never seen "a department official resist until he [Venecia] stood for everyone." However, some netizens don't approve of Venecia's statement and deems it as disobedient and irresponsible.

2967.author: Althea K. Lucente
2967.body:
The Supreme Court has indicted alleged pork barrel scam backer Sen. Alamano Mercado and four of his staff for helping to funnel in and out about 150 million pesos through casinos in public funds gained through a bribery and fraud scheme under Basic Development Assistance Fund (BDAF).

The Supreme Court said in a recently published statement that among those indicted for conspiring in domestic money laundering and plunder are:

[b]Marlon Sagun[/b] - 45, former senator, actor, and film star
[b]Billie D. Conese[/b] - 36, multi-corporation entrepreneur
[b]Venus Kaye Mamaril[/b] - 28, businesswoman, investor
[b]Morena Palma Kupitera[/b] - 59, former senator and film star

Three defendants, working with some 20 other officials, funneled into Mercado's ghost non-government organizations and non-profits from government funds especially including lawmakers' BDAF.

The National Commission of Investigation is already investigating a Chinese-Filipino, even before the hearing started, who allegedly played a key role in the laundering operation using a controversial loophole of the existing Anti-Money Laundering Law.

"We know there's still a considerable number of people out there involved in the BDAF scam, hiding, yet to be uncovered as we trace every document and dig through evidences dating back up to last year. Rest assured we will track you down and bring this deceit to a full stop. All I can say to them is, keep hiding as long as you could," said NCI Director Manny Longga.

In addition, Securities and Exchange Commission Director Harold Venecia has expressed fears that the Philippines may become a hotspot of money laundering where illegal circulation of money is concentrated. Venecia spoke up in an official statement where, amid hard times recovering from severe damages caused by The Ruling, he demands improvement in legislation, cleanliness, and transparency from the government executives. [url=https://liamsontimes.com.ph/2014/11/sec-director-venecia-2410]Learn more about this story here.[/url]

After being ruled unconstitutional last year by SC due to numerous loopholes such as external intervention and legal possibility of misuse, BDAF had finally been junked after almost 25 years of implementation into law. BDAF was intended for small-scale hard and soft projects that legislators themselves shall champion besides large-scale national projects, but only a fraction of the sum had been reportedly getting to the communities in need, especially those in rural and provincial areas.

7311.author: Kiko Espadero
7311.body:
At the province of Bayanan at Central Luzon, around 120 local fishermen and farmers assembled in front of their local Crisis Response Office Unit to speak out against the reckless and slow response to the calamity. Formerly a thriving home of fisheries and agriculture, their hope was wiped away by one of the eight localized earthquakes all over the nation during The Ruling.

Local fisherman Benedict Almosara, one of the organizers of the peaceful assembly, said "Are we that insignificant to be ignored? We live in a highly rural area with no buildings worth rebuilding. It has been months since our houses were torn apart and our children lost. If this were the capital, they would've cared, but we're just needy and we might not be worth their time. And what do they give us? Cops in riot gear instead of housing and jobs? We just want change."

Police and riot units were immediately deployed at the vicinity to prepare for potential escalation. Maj. Gen. Deporno Alat stated "The police force is ready for whatever happens to assure the utmost safety of our government officials and crisis response representatives."

The protest remained at ease from 10 o'clock in the morning until 6 o'clock in the evening. Two participants fainted under the scorching heat, who are currently in critical condition due to the 3-hour trip to the nearest medical unit. The provincial hospitals were wiped away by the earthquake and are still under renovation.

The Secretary of Health, Dr. Frankie Santos IX, previously announced that the renovation of provincial hospitals are still underway, but stated that their top priorities are vaccination of native ducks and breeding of mangoes and bananas, claiming that "it will have magical medical power."

1226.author: Althea K. Lucente
1226.body:
Following the reconstruction of highways and major roads, victims from the areas affected by the 8.2 magnitude earthquake in Makarito are now flocking to the capital for extensive healthcare and treatment.

Presidential spokesperson Roberto Quimpo announced the plans for highway reconstruction on September 8, 2014, boasting about the government's supposedly well-prioritized response to the February disaster known as The Ruling.

This follows Pres. Cojuangco's construction of Crisis Response Office Units (CROUs), which reportedly helped improve victims' living conditions and disseminate relief, but was criticized by experts for leaving access to healthcare in poor condition.

"They are all coming here because they believe they can finally get treatment for their injuries here," says Dr. Alvarez, director at Philippine General Hospital. "There have been no efforts to reconstruct public health infrastructure in the affected areas themselves," she added.

With hospitals at full capacity due to the sudden surge, Cojuangco continues to praise Health Secretary Frankie Santos IX for "doing his best," despite the steady rise of the death toll, which passed 402,000 in July.

1326.author: Kiko Espadero
1326.body:
Over a third of hospitals in NCR are close to full capacity as a surge of Ruling victims from the north arrive, brought about by the opening of newly reconstructed highways.

"We should expect the number of patients to continue to rise," Philippine General Hospital director Dr. Alvarez said. "We must prepare to work at full capacity. This means overtime for everyone working at the hospitals right now."

Patients are currently being denied admittance to hospitals to prioritize more serious cases, she explained. "We are also low on certain supplies and cannot readily attend to everyone in need."

Of the 56 public hospitals in NCR, 22 have reached "critical levels" of over 85% occupancy because of the rise in cases. Various outlets have reached out to and are waiting for a response from Health Sec. Frankie Santos IX, who recently traveled to Hawaii for further experimentation on the mango-banana hybrid experiment and for "other special occasions."

The government allocated a P49 billion rehabilitation fund for victims of the Ruling on February 12, and has since increased to P69 billion.

3744.author: Kenneth Aragones
3744.body:
In this day and age, the fact that discrimination is still an ongoing problem should not be ignored. This is what the youth leaders and volunteers of Love For All are calling attention to in their latest call to action.

"We've come a long way from the past," says volunteer Freya de Leon, "but there's still a lot of work to do before we can say we've achieved equality."

The country is said to be one of the LGBTQ+ friendly countries in the continent, but same-sex marriage is still out of the picture. Gay characters are still often the butt of jokes in media, and questioning youth often do not feel safe enough to come out.

"We're trying our best to foster a safe and welcoming environment for LGBTQ+ youth," says another volunteer, Diego Divinagracia. "We're trying to do our best to stick together and protect each other."

The Love For All group are collecting donations and recruiting members. You may reach them at loveforallyouth@email.com.

5432.author: Jillian Calangi
5432.body:
[b](Sponsored by Greenlife)[/b]

Evacuation centers celebrate hope and love in trying times with the help of donations and volunteers from Greenlife this Christmas.

The charity donated a Noche buena package for each family in every government-funded center in the capital.

Over 5,000 families were fed in an effort to nurture the country's Christmas spirit of giving and taking care of each other, despite the troubling times caused by the still unexplained The Ruling of this year.

This event is still deeply felt in areas of the country closest to the earthquakes' epicenters, with infrastructure yet to be reconstructed and citizens without homes.

Greenlife aims to make a difference and provide shelter for these victims with your support. To donate to these relief efforts, you may visit their official website for contact information or you may also deposit to their bank accounts directly.

Merry Christmas from Greenlife!

3531.author: Kenneth Aragones
3531.body:
The scene outside Paglaum General Hospital is bleak. There are lines of people outside, all with untreated injuries and ailments waiting for someone to help them. Johnrey is a 12-year-old boy with yellowed bandages haphazardly wrapped around his head. He sits with his father, whose crutches are made from pieces of wood and metal that had fallen in the earthquake. They wait.

Xyrie is a 14-year-old girl sitting at her younger sister's bedside. It had been 3 months since her little sister had been awake, 3 months since the last time Xyrie heard her laugh. Together, they wait.

According to articles from various small Filipino blogs, the Ruling was a one-time small-scale event and the after-effects of it are a hoax to control people with fear. If that's so, where are all these injuries coming from? Why are Johnrey and Xyrie still waiting? Who are we waiting for?

The truth is that there is a fake news epidemic that is affecting our country and its citizens. Dr. Tala San Juan of Philippine University said, "It's easy to dismiss these so-called news articles as outrageous, to think there's no way anybody would believe this. But it's happening all over the country now. People are beginning to believe that the effects of the Ruling are no longer a problem."

According to the study launched by the university, almost 30% of readers of these blogs seem to believe the articles they publish. While most are at the very least skeptical, this is quite an alarming number of believers.

Even some big name celebrities are not immune to the clutches of fake news. San Juan says, "It's far worse in their case because they have a platform. People look up to them and trust in their words, their perspectives. So when the everyday person sees their posts, they believe it."

Real people in the provinces continue to suffer. Hospitals have yet to be reconstructed. Evacuation centers are still overflowing, and kids like Johnrey and Xyrie are waiting.

This is the power of disinformation. This is the price of disinformation. As people insist that the effects of the Ruling are a hoax and the damage is far behind us, people die waiting for hope, waiting for help.

As a country, we must not let ourselves be fooled by fake news. We must look to where the real hurt is felt, and right now it is in the provinces, where real people need real help.

3220.author: Althea K. Lucente
3220.body:
This Christmas, President Cojuangco stayed true to his presidential campaign period roots and connected with the everyday man by enjoying a simple dinner with his most trusted family.

Known to his supporters for his reputation of being down-to-earth and relatable, he is often praised for his aversion to ostentatious displays of wealth and luxury.

"With a familiar and modest dinner in a pares house for Noche buena, joined only by his wife and kids, one can't help but be reminded of the regular working man's daily life, a far contrast to presidents before him," one netizen replied to the president's Nookface post.

Earlier this year, his daughter Margie Cojuangco was slammed for posting photos of a luxurious birthday party on a private island, a month after The Ruling took place.

Margie Cojuangco declined to comment.

1224.author: Sheila Sta. Maria
1224.body:
[b](Sponsored by ForeverColor)[/b]

This Christmas, separate yourself from the normies and stay on fleek with ForeverColor's Festive Collection!

Boasting iconic Christmas colors like a shimmering golden glitter eyeshadow and seasonal true red lippie, you'll be far from basic if you grab this gorgeous limited edition three-color palette and lippie.

ForeverColor is a locally-made cosmetics brand birthed from the dreams of local SheEO Amber de la Cruz, who wants the girls of this generation to feel beautiful and powerful as they achieve their dreams.

"The feminist wave has only been growing stronger," she says in a social media post about the launch. "I want the young women of our country to know there's nothing wrong with aiming high and achieving their career goals—all while wearing a bright red lip."

The Festive Collection is available from December 15, 2014 to January 31, 2015, in select department stores nationwide.

2535.author: Sheila Sta. Maria
2535.body:
In February this year, the series of natural disasters known as The Ruling caused mass death and destruction all over the country. The events are most known for the massive earthquakes, but these also led to tsunamis and floods especially in areas such as Eastern Visayas.

The local government units are ramping up efforts and have partnered with non-profits and volunteer-led organizations to build small communities to house victims.

"National relief operations have been mostly concentrated in Luzon," says activist Pepe Cañete. "We have had to organize donation drives, evacuation efforts, and medical care ourselves."

Despite the lack of funding and aid from national government, the efforts of the LGUs and volunteers in the affected areas have seen tremendous effects already.

"There are still plenty of municipalities that are deemed unsafe, but we have been able to provide housing and basic utilities for a big chunk of the victims."

Since the incident, around 500 families in the area have been housed, with more communities still being built.

2000.author: Jillian Calangi
2000.body:
In a press conference this afternoon by Vice Pres. Fiona Diosdado, she reiterated the significance of resilience and unity among the Filipino people and expressed her deepest sympathies towards those families whose lives and worlds were "rolled" by The Ruling. This opening speech went on for a prolonged six hours before the press were allowed to ask questions.

When asked about the possible disclosure of how the P69B rehabilitation funds were utilized in an alleged period of one week, Diosdado replied "No comment," after which Diosdado repeated her opening speech as her closing speech for another six hours.

Despite the construction of Crisis Response Office Units (CROUs), housing, and clinics, ongoing protests around the nation demand reconstruction and reopening of damaged hospitals and rejuvenation of healthcare services in affected regions.

On February 16, 2014, Pres. Cojuangco allotted a P69 billion worth of rehabilitation funds for areas affected by The Ruling. Despite concerns and pressure from senators, Pres. Cojuangco acted alone and handed the responsibility of the utilization of rehabilitation funds to VP Diosdado, duly assigned as the Financial Director of The Ruling Inter-Agency Task Force (TRIATF).

2001.author: Kiko Espadero
2001.body:
In a press conference held by the Office of the Vice President (OVP), VP Fiona Diosdado opened with an hour-long speech about the "ever-growing need" for Filipino resilience and unity, likening Filipinos to glitters, gold, and shooting stars. "You'll never shine if you don't glow," she said.

When asked about the continued shortage of the increasing need for healthcare services in Central Luzon and parts of Visayas, Diosdado replied "No comment."

All other questions that followed obtained the exact same response from Diosdado, perplexing the press and attendees. Diosdado eventually walked out of the conference without notice.

Prof. Harry Romano, a linguistics professor at Valino University, suggests this may be a rare bad case of what's known as "semantic satiation," where a short string of words or a phrase such as "no comment" loses its meaning to its speaker due to over-repetition. "This realization, this loss of meaning, you know, it may have gravely disturbed the vice president," Romano claimed.

OVP Asst. Sec. Garci Gloria reported later after the conference that the vice president is "well and safe."

2002.author: George Ferrer
2002.body:
The Office of the Vice President (OVP) held a press conference this afternoon with The Ruling rehabilitation and recovery plans on the agenda. OVP Asst. Sec. Garci Gloria opened the conference this time, citing the surrounding "recent health concerns" of the vice president, and reassuring the public that VP Diosdado is healthy.

Despite initial concerns regarding her "lapse," Gloria reported that the VP's recovery was immediate after finding out about the politician's approval ratings going up by 3%. "We were all relieved when she finally said something else," he reported. "The vice president's first words were: I only serve the people."

Gloria started the press conference by announcing the OVP's new ambitious plans. He reported that the construction plans for the yet-to-be-named Philippine space agency are underway. "This will inspire us to be more resilient and united," he claimed. Plans include launching surveillance satellites and, one day, to "go for the moon."

The Ruling rehabilitation, the original agenda of the press con, was not touched upon.

Netizens have caught up on VP Diosdado's unusual repetition of the phrase "no comment" and has been trending on social media platforms with the hashtag "#NoComment", typically making fun of the VP's defensive remark. Other hashtags like #NoProgress and #NoCommentDanceChallenge are also trending.

8343.author: Sheila Sta. Maria
8343.body:
World economy has yet to show signs of recovery after the disastrous impact of The Ruling, United Countries Department of Economic and Social Affairs released a report on Monday, citing business activity and global employment indicators barely moving since the crash in February 2014.

UC DESA has expressed grave concern over the global economic stagnation, highlighting the limited success of programs around the world focusing on rehabilitation and job creation.

"This new analysis underscores the ongoing economic hardship caused by The Ruling," said UC DESA Chief Economist Masamuri Takeda. "While some policies enacted by governments and the WBDO may have cushioned the blow, the lack of significant recovery is alarming. These findings highlight the need for urgent and innovative interventions."

The Ruling triggered the recession earlier this year causing the global economy to suffer $53.2 trillion in losses—equivalent to 13.6% to 17.1% of global domestic product (GDP).

World Bank De Oro (WBDO) forecasts a period of minimal movement in the upcoming year, with potential growth ranging from a negligible 0.5% to a modest 3%.

However, the debt-to-GDP ratio of third-world countries is expected to remain dangerously high, predicted to average over 90% of their GDP. The UC DESA report indicates this is due to ongoing fiscal policies that continue to weaken macroeconomic fundamentals.

9127.author: Jillian Calangi
9127.body:
A nationwide assessment reveals a concerning need for repairs in approximately 75% of school buildings across the country, from primary to higher education. The crisis underscores the combined impact of the recent northern earthquake and a nationwide issue of aging educational infrastructure.

The report, commissioned by the Department of Education (DE), highlights damage caused by the earthquake nine months ago. The quake severely impacted several regions, and many schools in those areas remain unsafe where structural weaknesses, both obvious and hidden, pose risks.

However, the report also paints a picture of widespread deterioration even in areas unaffected by the earthquake. Cracked walls and foundations, worsened by seismic activity, are the primary safety hazard in areas affected by The Ruling. On the other hand, in unaffected areas, the report points to lack of maintenance and aging infrastructure as the cause.

"This isn't good," stated Education Undersecretary Flower Gutierrez. "Yeah, this isn't ideal."

Fears of classrooms collapsing are not uncommon among parents. "I take my son to school every day. The cracks on the walls seem like they're growing," said one parent at Yamang Elementary School. "I fear this poses a real threat to our children."

4090.author: George Ferrer
4090.body:
Government employees working in several historic government buildings, mostly constructed in the early to mid-1900s, are being evacuated starting today following growing concerns about structural safety. The evacuation comes months after The Ruling earthquake shook the north and, to some extent, the National Capital Region (NCR).

Engineers have been assessing the buildings since the earthquake, and their reports have consistently indicated the need for urgent and immediate action to repair potential safety hazards. Despite this, government officials have repeatedly delayed repair efforts, arguing that their operations cannot be disrupted as "entire industries would be negatively affected."

Two days ago, four people working in the Central Post Office (CPO) were gravely injured after a sudden structural collapse in one part of the building. As of writing, they are still receiving treatment at the Philippine General Hospital.

"The safety of our government workers is paramount," stated CPO President Tracy Dimagiba. "While these buildings hold historical significance, we cannot risk the lives of our workers."

Despite initial pushback from government officials, this serious incident has incited immediate action to start evacuating government employees.

"I don't want to say ‘I told you so,' you know?" said Engr. Renz Rivera. "But it seems like we really only take action once something happens."

9501.author: Seth Llanera
9501.body:
All KRT-3 stations have been shut down following an incident currently being investigated by the rapid transit line's officials and engineers.

17 people sustained light to moderate injuries due to the train cars' sudden braking. They were immediately brought to the nearest hospital, while the rest of the passengers were forced to walk on the rail tracks under the 2 pm heat.

It's been only one month since the KRT-3 reopened after repairs to delayed structural damages caused by The Ruling earthquake.

"We regrettably have to do this for everyone's safety," said KRTA Spokesperson Johnoy Ricardo. "We will make sure to check every corner again and repair the damages."

Since the closure, students and workers have complained about the increased difficulty of commuting and worsening traffic congestion.

"It was already hard before, but now I have to leave the house three hours ahead of time to get to school," said PU student Marissa Colmenares. "Some professors are more understanding than others."

KRT-1 and KRT-2 remain in operation.
